description: Scenario-keyed sabotage matrix for the required-tools preflight. Each scenario names one deliberately induced proxy state, the SURFACE it is observed on, the disclosure TIER it is observed at, and the EXACT per-tool verdict it must produce: status, reason, retryable and action (an omitted action means the reason carries none). The set-level verdict and CLI exit code are the ones a single-tool request of that shape must report. A request that is REJECTED rather than evaluated carries request_error instead of a verdict, and a row on the mcp-plain surface carries plain_error, that surface's per-id error code, because plain describe_tool has its own vocabulary. internal/server/preflight_e2e_test.go drives the REST rows against a real mcpproxy binary, internal/server/preflight_mcp_check_matrix_test.go drives every mcp-check and mcp-plain row, and reflection checks fail if any code of the 15-code enum has no REST row or no mcp-check row (excepting the two codes that are REST-only by design).

surfaces.e2e: induced against a running mcpproxy binary with sabotaged fixture upstreams, observed over POST /api/v1/preflight
surfaces.state-injected: induced by injecting the connection-state snapshot the runtime cannot be forced into deterministically from outside
surfaces.mcp-check: observed in band through describe_tool with check:true (spec 099); always the agent-token tier
surfaces.mcp-plain: observed in band through describe_tool WITHOUT check, whose per-id vocabulary is not_found|quarantined|pending_approval|changed|disabled

scenarios.sabotage: none: indexed, approved tool on an enabled, healthy, trusted server — asserted both unfiltered and under each of the three annotation filters, since a fully annotated tool must survive all of them
POST /api/v1/servers/{server}/quarantine on a previously healthy, indexed server
rewrite the upstream tool's description in the fixture tools file, then restart the server so the proxy re-lists it (rug-pull guard trips)
add a tool to the fixture tools file after the trusted server's baseline was auto-approved, then restart the server
POST /api/v1/servers/{server}/tools/block for one tool
server configured with disabled_tools containing the requested tool
server configured with enabled:false
arm the fixture's fail-switch file, SIGKILL the upstream process, then force a reconnect: the restarted fixture exits immediately, so the server settles in a stable non-connected state

restart an already-indexed server with a long initialize delay, so it sits in connecting/discovering while its tools remain in the shared index; see never_indexed_while_connecting for the case where the tool was never indexed at all — the connection-state verdict wins there too
policy.read_only_only against a tool whose upstream definition declares no annotations
policy.exclude_destructive against a tool with no destructiveHint and no read-only hint
policy.exclude_open_world against a tool with no openWorldHint
policy.read_only_only against a tool explicitly annotated readOnlyHint:false
policy.exclude_destructive against a tool explicitly annotated destructiveHint:true
policy.exclude_open_world against a tool explicitly annotated openWorldHint:true
misspelled tool name on a configured, healthy server
tool id naming a server that is not configured at all
pin_hash at the current schema version whose digest does not match the tool's stored hash
pin_hash carrying the tool's CURRENT digest under a different hash schema version (simulates a proxy-side hash-algorithm bump)
connection-state snapshot reports the deferred-OAuth PendingAuth state for the server
preflight under a profile whose server list excludes the requested tool's server, called with the operator API key

same out-of-scope request as profile_out_of_scope_operator, called with an agent token whose allowed_servers excludes the server: scope-silence maps it to a plain not_found, byte-indistinguishable from an absent tool

a configured, enabled server that has NEVER been indexed, with the connection-state snapshot reporting connecting: existence is unknowable while the server is not Ready, so the connection verdict wins over not_found (FR-005 — corrects the note the mid_indexing row used to carry)
none: indexed, approved tool on an enabled, healthy, trusted server, checked in band with describe_tool check:true
the requested tool's server is quarantined, checked in band
the requested tool's server is configured enabled:false, checked in band
the tool carries a spec-032 approval record in the pending state, checked in band
the tool's approval record is in the changed (rug-pull) state, checked in band
the tool's approval record is disabled by the user, checked in band
the server's disabled_tools denylist contains the requested tool, checked in band
misspelled tool name on a configured, in-scope server, checked in band
an id with no '<server>:<tool>' separator: a per-id verdict with a format hint, never a batch failure, checked in band
tool id naming a server that is not configured at all: at the in-band tier server_not_configured collapses to a plain not_found, byte-indistinguishable from an unknown id (spec 099 FR-009)

tool on a server outside the session's scope (agent-token allowed_servers or active profile): server_not_in_scope collapses to the SAME not_found, so a probe cannot learn what sits behind the scope (spec 099 FR-009/SC-007)
connection-state snapshot reports the deferred-OAuth PendingAuth state for the server, projected onto the in-band payload
connection-state snapshot reports the server in the error state, projected onto the in-band payload
connection-state snapshot reports the server connecting while its tools are still indexed, projected onto the in-band payload
filters.read_only_only against a tool whose upstream definition declares no annotations
filters.exclude_destructive against a tool whose upstream definition declares no annotations
filters.exclude_open_world against a tool whose upstream definition declares no annotations
filters.read_only_only against a tool explicitly annotated as unsafe for that filter
filters.exclude_destructive against a tool explicitly annotated as unsafe for that filter
filters.exclude_open_world against a tool explicitly annotated as unsafe for that filter
exactly 50 raw ids in one check-mode call: all 50 are evaluated and every ready tool answers ready (the cap applies to the raw array, before trimming and dedup)
51 raw ids in one check-mode call
a `filters` object sent without check:true — silently ignoring it would let an agent believe a safety filter was applied when it was not
the reserved `expect_hashes` field sent in any shape: rejected rather than ignored, so in-band pins stay additive (spec 099 FR-008)

describe_tool WITHOUT check for a tool on a server outside the session's scope: the retired `invisible` code is replaced by not_found, whose remediation was already the shared not-found text (spec 099 FR-011)

rest_only_reasons.hash_mismatch: in-band hash pins were trimmed from spec 099 v1 (FR-008): nothing in band can request a pin, so nothing in band can fail one
rest_only_reasons.server_not_in_scope: the whole in-band surface is the agent-token tier (spec 099 FR-009), where this collapses to not_found
rest_only_reasons.server_not_configured: the whole in-band surface is the agent-token tier (spec 099 FR-009), where this collapses to not_found — see mcp_check_unknown_server, which asserts the collapse
